then.text: Did the sacking fit? Dundee jute went everywhere: sandbags in two world wars, wagon covers in the American West, sacks for coffee and sugar all over the world.

else.text: Sacking for the Discovery's stores? We can do that. Jute's tough, cheap and it doesn't mind the cold.
Take these hanks of fibre. And here's how the spinners twisted it into twine, if you fancy making snares of your own.
This was a jute mill. Raw jute came from Bengal, was softened with whale oil, then carded, spun and woven. The noise was so loud the workers learnt to lip-read.
At its height Dundee had dozens of mills and tens of thousands of jute workers. Most of them women and girls, some no older than you'd be starting high school.
